state.requirement: Perform unattended Batch 17 round 2 closeout for M9-T23 and M9-T29. First reproduce every bug, fix only its root cause, retain red/green regression evidence, and use Jev for ordinary technical forks. M9-T23 AC5 forbids reading /snapshot or starting another login probe when agent.availability_changed reason=login_changed arrives. AC6 requires the zero-output approval card to show authoritative current login context and preserve rerun, reassign, and reject behavior. The frontend is a presentation and API mapping layer, not a policy authority.

task.title: Refresh a waiting zero-output approval card after the daemon login probe completes
task.accept: The mounted approval card must update from unchecked login to the newly probed timestamp without user navigation, a global snapshot read, another login/model probe, or changing gate/run state. Old cards with null context remain compatible. Late overlapping reads or an unmounted container must not restore obsolete gate context.

state.conflict: The original real native provider suite at clean head 1b0c75d932fbb38ff3f3696a90df0ae9a547f815 passed valid-model R17-CONTROL content and the 16-second SIGSTOP startup-budget control. A nonexistent model then exited before output. GET /gates showed a newly checked login timestamp after refreshLogin, while the browser gate login badge title stayed em dash; original e2e line 779 failed without any assertion changes. run.ts commits and publishes gate/run exit before awaiting refreshLogin. agents.ts clears the login cache at probe start and publishes login_changed only after storing the result. gates.ts resolves current login dynamically at GET time. RunDeckContainer loads gates on run/lane/task milestones but ignores agent.availability_changed. Its gates live in private React state; cache-invalidation has no gates resource. Calling the existing full load() on login_changed would violate AC5 by rereading /snapshot. This is an authorized local seam fix across M9-T23 and its M9-T20/M9-T21 container predecessors, not a feature or canonical contract change.

options.A: Add a focused ordinary GET /gates refresh in the existing RunDeckContainer subscription, only for login_changed. Share in-flight gate reads, refresh a read invalidated after it starts, retain the latest authoritative gate result across overlapping full deck loads, and clean up on unmount. Update only gate presentation state. Keep cache-invalidation mappings, global snapshots, probe calls, gate creation, and action rules unchanged. Add mounted DOM regressions for probe completion and overlapping stale reads, with negative assertions on snapshot/probe requests, then rerun the unchanged real provider suite.
options.B: Use the authoritative login field already carried by login_changed to update context.login only on currently loaded gates whose referenced RunDto.agentId matches that event. Track later login events while full deck loads are pending so old results cannot overwrite them. Never create a missing legacy context or infer a login policy. This avoids an extra GET /gates but adds a frontend projection joining event payloads, run identity, and gate context. Add mounted DOM and race regressions with negative request assertions, then rerun the unchanged real provider suite.
options.C: Preserve product code, retain the native suite failure as an open S2 repair task with this production reproduction, and complete the closeout record and other evidence without claiming AC6/provider recovery passed. This is safe but leaves the known local seam unresolved even though the user authorized root-cause fixes.

task.title: Complete the current native production suite's Batch 17 density evidence
task.accept: Every required route and viewport has the unchanged density probe result using the current section 11 page type and padding contract. Pairing is probed before entering its code, normal authenticated routes are reached through UI pairing, and connection failure is caused by a real unused API port selected through the existing UI address control. No mock routes, injected token/storage state, synthetic event, or reduced probe threshold is used.

state.conflict: The existing native provider suite already measures agents (work, pad18), pipeline (form, pad18) and deck (work) at all three viewports. Its maintained density helper currently accepts only work/form. The round's requested devices, landing, run detail, missing-run, pair and connection-failed results are not produced by that suite. Prior historical density evidence cannot establish the current whole batch. The user permits only the batch worktree and planning directory and requires the native GIF to come from one fresh run. Environment failures are kept separately, including a recent global GIT_INDEX_FILE leaking to nested acceptance Git projects; that run is not acceptance evidence and the environment is being corrected without changing product code.

options.A: Extend only the maintained native E2E evidence helper to accept the existing card type and add state-waited probes for missing required routes within the same fresh provider flow. Pair before typing the code; reach devices/landing/run through normal authenticated navigation; measure connection failure last using the existing pairing-page Save Manual Address control to persist a real unused port followed by normal reload. Keep all original assertions and limits, reset viewport before each published frame, and rerun from a clean exact head. This adds persistent acceptance coverage and may expose real layout failures, which must be reported or fixed with red/green evidence rather than relaxed.
options.B: Keep the native suite unchanged and run a separate planning-only production density harness that boots the same exact head with normal registry inputs and pairs another isolated browser through the public flow. Measure all missing routes and real unreachable-address failure there; publish the original native-flow GIF and explicitly separate the two run provenances. Preserve all original provider assertions. This avoids changes to maintained tests but duplicates setup and leaves future CI without full Batch 17 density coverage.
